neighbours.label: talk of repaying borrowed money (pay back, paid back with interest, repaid, a way to pay the loan), not other senses of pay
fire: The farmer borrowed from the bank and paid back the money in three years.
Graduates often spend decades repaying what they borrowed for college.
She lent him a thousand dollars and he never paid her back.
The city must repay the bonds with interest by 2030.
Borrowers who cannot pay back the loan may lose their homes.
He took out a mortgage and has to pay it off over thirty years.
The firm borrowed heavily and could not repay its creditors.
A pawnbroker expects the sum to be paid back within a month.
quiet: The farmer visited the bank and paid a call on the manager in May.
Graduates often spend decades paying attention to their old college.
She met him at a dinner and he paid her a kind compliment.
The city must pay its bus drivers more money by 2030.
Workers who are paid on Friday may visit their homes.
He took out the trash and paid no attention to the noise.
The firm hired heavily and paid its cleaners by the hour.
A waiter expects the bill to be paid at the end of a meal.

notes: Card: ' pay' x9, ' paid' x4, ' back' x3, ' loan', ' payment', ' recovered'. Probes: 'paid back with interest' 1.242, 'repaid' 0.901, 'pay this money back' 0.614, 'no way to pay it' 0.342; 'pay a visit' 0.110, 'got paid on Friday' 0.014, 'paid a compliment' 0.011.
